name: Maan Aluminium Ltd
title: Maan Aluminium Ltd - 532906 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Maan Aluminium FY26 revenue flat at INR809 crore, PBT down 18% to INR18 crore; utilisation of new capacity ramp delayed, margin recovery pushed out ~2 years.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was almost flat at INR809 crore versus INR810 crore, while EBITDA rose 3% to INR31 crore on better operational controls and value-added mix. PBT fell 18% to INR18 crore and PAT fell 19% to INR13 crore, hit by higher raw material prices, lower exports, energy costs and gas supply curbs. Net worth rose 54% to INR274 crore after an INR83 crore preferential issue. Management said the new Italian press at Pithampur (extrusion capacity 10,000 to 24,000 tpa) is built but utilisation has lagged, and FY27 is expected to be flat on volumes.

financial_highlights.change: +54% vs INR178 crore, driven by INR83 crore preferential raise and retained profit

financial_highlights.metric: Blended EBITDA per ton (value-added and extrusion)
financial_highlights.value: approx. $300 per ton (about 280 per ton as stated by management)
financial_highlights.change: stated figures were inconsistent during Q&A

segments.name: Extrusion and value-added (manufacturing)
segments.commentary: FY26 manufacturing sales realisation about INR300 crore on roughly 7,300 MT; extrusion realisation about $340 per ton EBITDA-equivalent on a blended basis (management clarified $340, not INR340, per ton). Value-added products (anodizing, powder coating, machining, tubing) said to carry margins around 25% above extrusion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 50% of manufacturing revenue (approx. INR150 crore). US accounts for 80-85% of exports; US duty on aluminium products at 50% since 2024. Exports down 30-40% over three years, 10-15% per year; Gulf dispatches halted since the war-related insurance terrorism clause invocation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 described as a flat year for volumes; expected next-year volumes around 7,000-7,500 MT.
Target to reach at least 75% utilisation of 24,000 tpa capacity within three years (15-20% annual market capture cited).
FY27 ramp-up and depreciation, finance and employee costs expected to add INR7-10 crore plus another INR10 crore in FY27.
Normalised margins now expected about two years out (around FY28), pushed back from earlier FY27 plans.
Capex guided at INR40-50 crore for FY27 and INR30-40 crore (stated as INR35-40 crore) for FY28.

Dewas precision tube line expected to reach 40-50% utilisation within a few years once machinery renegotiation closes; management said FY26 was not great and benefits from utilisation expected next year or the year after.
capex_capacity: Italian extrusion press commissioned at Pithampur, raising extrusion capacity from 10,000 to 24,000 tpa; press suited to 2-, 5- and 7-series alloys for EV, defence and aerospace.

Dewas facility acquired and refurbished; precision tube line planned, but project delayed by cost increases and renegotiation with overseas machinery vendors; equipment lead time about eight months plus six to eight months for approvals.
Management is seeking technology partner or JV for Dewas operations; nothing finalised.
Advances to customers of INR16.4 crore in non-current assets relate mainly to a Delhi office purchase, not Dewas machinery, per management.
demand_pricing: Aluminium commodity prices up more than 50%, raising raw material costs; cost pass-through for raw material is possible, but operating cost increases cannot be passed on immediately.
Customers have slowed or deferred orders due to US tariffs combined with higher metal prices; Gulf dispatches halted; containers constrained.
Inquiry pipeline reported robust in defence, aerospace, solar and engineering; defence tier-one qualification audit expected within six months.
Contracts are open-ended with no fixed-term supply commitments; NDAs in place; export shift to CIS markets and FOB Incoterms being negotiated.
Competitors named as Jindal and Hindalco extrusions, described as volume-based; Maan positions itself on OEM and value-added niche.
Tata-related business: sampling complete, first qualification submitted, second batch to go in June 2026; management expects it to materialise this year, though it did not disclose names.

qa_highlights.question: Volumes, revenue and EBITDA for extrusion in Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 volume about 7,300 MT; sales realisation about INR300 crore total; EBITDA about $300-340 per ton blended (figure given inconsistently during the call).

qa_highlights.question: Ramp-up of extrusion and value-added mix going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 flat; target 75% capacity utilisation within three years; value-added margins about 25% above extrusion; aspiration of higher per-ton EBITDA not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Cost increase expected in FY27 from capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up costs of INR7-10 crore plus another INR10 crore from depreciation, finance cost, employee cost and trials.

qa_highlights.question: Why gross margin fell to around 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs passed through, but operating and energy costs not immediately recoverable; fixed-cost absorption weak due to low utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Dewas facility products and scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Precision drawing tube line for import substitution; project delayed by cost overrun; 40-50% utilisation expected eventually; no pricing or EBITDA per ton guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 INR40-50 crore; FY28 INR30-40 crore (confirmed range).

risks_watch: Utilisation of 24,000 tpa capacity remains low; FY27 flat, with margin normalisation pushed out to about two years.
Export dependence on the US (80-85% of exports) under 50% duty; Gulf logistics disrupted.
Dewas project cost overruns and renegotiation; no technology partner yet.
Gross margin compression (about 8% per analyst cited) and inability to pass on operating and energy costs immediately.
Management's FY26 EBITDA-per-ton figures were stated inconsistently, so verify disclosure before modelling.
Tata-linked business qualification and June 2026 second batch; defence audit within six months.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management called FY26 'not great' and declined to give hard numbers or near-term hopes, while stressing capacity is built and the issue is utilisation timing. Confidence rests on pipeline and value-added strategy rather than near-term financial recovery.
key_quotes: The challenge is primarily one of timing and utilization rather than capability creation.
I think the year '26 was not great. Actually, maybe the end of '26 was not great. I don't want to give any false hopes or anything.
So, this year we are going to see a very flat year. That's what we feel.

adds.what: Italian extrusion press at Pithampur raising extrusion capacity from 10,000 to 24,000 tpa (commissioned, utilisation lagging)
Dewas precision tube line (acquired and refurbished; machinery renegotiation pending, ~8 months equipment lead time plus 6-8 months approvals)

growth.why: FY27 guided flat at ~7,000-7,500 MT volumes (FY26 revenue flat at INR809 crore) as the newly commissioned Pithampur press (10,000 to 24,000 tpa) ramps slowly; the 75% utilisation target is three years out and Dewas is delayed, with normalised margins pushed to about FY28.
